SK9027 A compilation unit was cancelled, so the run saw only part of the tree

A compilation unit was cancelled before it finished and contributed no findings, so the run saw only part of the tree. The reliability gate fails on it unconditionally, under every gate definition, and skala baseline create / update refuse to write from such a run. Re-run without cancelling; there is no flag that accepts it.

CategoryTool
Default severitywarning
ScopeCompilation
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileno — it reads the whole compilation
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

A cancelled unit returns zero findings while every other unit reports normally, so partial: true legitimately appears beside a large finding count — a sweep observed it next to 211 findings and could not account for it (#309). The run-level flag stays aggregate because the gate needs one answer, and this diagnostic names the unit so the reader does not have to trace it by hand. A baseline written from a partial run would accept the silence of whatever did not run, and every later run would compare against it.

When it does not fire

None; the analyzer host sets the flag in exactly one place, its cancellation handler. The gate fails on the run's flag rather than on this diagnostic, so it fails even when the diagnostic is absent, with a less specific message. Distinct from SK9030, an analyzer that threw and was disabled: that is also a reliability failure, but per rule rather than per unit.
